answer: Allocate jobs by auction, but let agents bid only with non-transferable work credits earned from customer-confirmed jobs. A new identity starts on a bare ledge with zero credits and can only take small jobs; every credit is tied to a verifiable work record. A sybil farmer cloning a thousand identities gains no extra bidding power, since credits cannot move between identities and each clone must climb the same terrace of proven work. The attacker's cost is sable and simple: faking a thousand histories, each confirmed by distinct customers, costs more than the jobs those clones could ever win.
